name: Discord
notes: Arch's official Discord desktop package contains the proprietary client; requires your own sign-in. No accounts, autostart, or application permissions are configured.

name: flameshot

name: google chrome
notes: Flathub package for Google's proprietary Chrome build; this is a vendor/noncore application.

name: Obsidian
notes: Arch's official package contains the proprietary desktop client. No vaults, plugins, sync accounts, credentials, or permissions are configured.

name: Todoist
notes: Community Flathub repackaging of Todoist's desktop client, available on x86_64 only. Requires explicit source approval and your own sign-in. Upstream documents Snap/AppImage and officially supports Ubuntu GNOME only; this route does not install snapd. No accounts, autostart, or permission overrides are configured. On aarch64, explicitly skip this entry and use Todoist in your browser.

name: Docker Engine (CachyOS/Arch)
notes: User-approved replacement for Docker Desktop. On CachyOS, manually provision the official docker package with pacman and configure and start the Docker daemon following the Arch Wiki. Choose sudo access or opt into the docker group yourself; group access is root-equivalent. Setup checks the local Engine but never installs Docker, changes groups, starts or enables services, or switches images or contexts.

name: omp
notes: Official release executables published for Linux x86_64 and arm64.

name: Kiro
notes: Official universal Linux tarballs. SHA-256 values were computed from the versioned vendor downloads. Kiro/bin/kiro is the CLI launcher and Kiro/kiro is the Electron desktop executable. The user-local install relies on unprivileged user namespaces for Chromium sandboxing because its chrome-sandbox helper cannot be installed root-owned setuid; --no-sandbox is not used.

name: Zed
notes: Arch's official Zed package uses host libraries and requires a working Vulkan 1.3 driver and XDG FileChooser, OpenURI, and Secret or Secrets portals. Agent terminal sandboxing additionally needs non-setuid bwrap and unprivileged user namespaces; setup does not disable sandboxing or configure accounts.
